title: The Cat That Chose Us
text:
We did not choose our cat. Our cat chose us, which is a very different thing.
She appeared one evening at the kitchen window, thin and filthy, with one ear torn from some fight we would never know about. My mother said firmly that we were not keeping her. Then she put out a saucer of milk.
The cat came back the next night, and the night after that. Within a fortnight she had claimed the armchair by the window, and within a month my mother was buying a particular brand of fish that no other cat in Singapore apparently found acceptable.
She has lived with us for six years now. She still will not sit on anybody's lap, and she still bolts at the sound of the door.
But every evening at nine o'clock, she walks into my mother's room and sleeps at the foot of the bed, and my mother, who was never keeping her, leaves the door open.
